name: Clojure
title: Clojure (1.12)

type.text: **Protocols decouple behaviour from inheritance**: `defprotocol` declares a set of functions, and `extend-type` and `extend-protocol` implement them for any type, including Java classes and `nil`, so behaviour is added without a class hierarchy
**Dynamic typing defers every type check to run time**: A function declares no parameter or return type, so a mismatch is found when the value is used
**Protocol dispatch resolves at run time**: The implementation is chosen from the value's type when the call executes, and a type with no implementation fails then

**No sum types and no generics**: Alternatives are tagged maps or `:type` keywords by convention, and a function accepts any value, so neither the case set nor the argument shape is checked by the compiler (T4, T5)
**Operator names are ordinary vars**: `+` and `=` can be shadowed in a namespace or a local binding, so a reader resolves the symbol from the current scope
**`clojure.spec` checks a boundary on demand**: A spec declares the shape of arguments and results, and `instrument` turns it into a run-time assertion where a program chooses to

construction.text: **Immutable structures decouple a change from its readers**: `assoc`, `conj`, and `update` return a new value and leave the old one intact, so a reader that holds the earlier value sees no change
**Persistent structures share their unchanged parts**: A vector, map, or set update copies only the changed path, so immutability does not cost a full copy
**`let` scopes a binding to its form**: A value's lifetime is its lexical form, so construction does not depend on a declaration elsewhere
**Records separate data from behaviour**: `defrecord` gives an associative value with named fields, and plain functions operate on it without a class that owns them
**Macros extend the surface syntax without changing the core**: `defmacro` transforms forms at compile time, so a domain notation is added outside the language
**Top-level `def` state is globally visible**: A `def` or `defonce` var is reachable from every namespace, and `alter-var-root` can rebind it, so shared state needs discipline

memory.text: **The JVM garbage collector pauses the program**: Reclamation timing is the collector's decision, so a latency-sensitive path cannot assume a bound
**No RAII**: Destruction is not tied to scope, and `finalize` and `java.lang.ref.Cleaner` are unreliable, so release must be explicit
**No ownership model**: A value can be referenced from anywhere on the heap, and the collector reclaims it only after the last reference disappears
**Immutable values make sharing safe**: Because a value cannot change in place, handing the same reference to another thread cannot alter the first holder's view
**`with-open` releases a resource at scope exit**: The macro expands to `try`/`finally`, so a file, socket, or stream is closed even on an exception
**Direct buffers keep bulk data off the managed heap**: `java.nio.ByteBuffer.allocateDirect` and primitive arrays reduce collector pressure on large payloads

error.text: **Exceptions are unchecked**: A JVM exception propagates without declaration, so a function's failure set is not visible in its signature
**`ex-info` carries a data map**: `ex-info` attaches a map that `ex-data` reads, so a handler inspects structured context instead of parsing a message
**`try`/`catch`/`finally` separates the recovery path**: Recovery code sits in a dedicated form beside the normal path
**Function preconditions and postconditions are declarative**: `:pre` and `:post` in a `defn` attribute map check a call and its result at run time
**A failure surfaces only when the value is used**: With no declared types there is no compile-time list of what a call can raise

concurrency.text: **Immutable data is the default**: A value shared between threads cannot be changed by another thread, so most data needs no lock
**Atoms give uncoordinated synchronous change**: `swap!` updates one reference with compare-and-set semantics and `reset!` stores a value outright, independent of every other reference
**Refs and `dosync` give coordinated STM transactions**: `alter` inside a transaction commits all its references atomically or retries, so a multi-reference change is isolated and composable
**Agents give asynchronous serialised updates**: `send` and `send-off` queue an action, and each agent runs its actions in order
**`core.async` channels decouple producers from consumers**: `chan` and `go` blocks transfer values without shared mutable state
**A transaction can retry its body**: A conflicting `dosync` block runs again, so a side effect inside it may happen more than once

platform.text: **Full access to the JVM ecosystem**: `import`, `proxy`, and `gen-class` let Clojure call any Java library directly
**ClojureScript compiles the same language to JavaScript**: The Google Closure compiler targets the browser and Node.js from the same source
**`.cljc` reader conditionals share code across hosts**: One file selects host-specific forms at read time, so common logic stays in one place
**JVM start-up precedes `main`**: A command-line run pays the JVM initialisation cost before the program executes
**Host interop couples a namespace to its host**: A namespace that imports `java.util.Date` cannot run on ClojureScript unless the host-specific parts are isolated

performance.text: **JIT warm-up precedes peak speed**: HotSpot interprets first and compiles hot paths later, so a short-lived process may never reach peak throughput
**Hot paths reach native speed**: On a long-running service the JIT compiles the hot loops to machine code
**Persistent structures keep update cost logarithmic**: An update shares the unchanged parts, so immutability does not multiply allocation
**Transients build a collection in place**: `transient` and `persistent!` construct a large collection without intermediate copies where it is not yet shared
**Boxing and reflection cost throughput**: Untyped arithmetic boxes numbers, and a reflective Java call resolves at run time unless a type hint (`^`) is present
**Start-up is slow**: JVM initialisation and namespace loading make a short command-line program slower than a native binary

ecosystem.text: **The library base is small beside Java and npm**: The number of available libraries is a fraction of those ecosystems
**The whole JVM library base is reachable**: A `deps.edn` or Leiningen project resolves Maven artifacts, so Java libraries are used directly
**Clojars and Maven give dependency management**: Resolution, versioning, and publishing are tooled and reproducible
**The core library is small and deliberate**: `clojure.core` is stable and rarely needs a breaking change
**Build conventions differ between teams**: Leiningen, `deps.edn`/`tools.deps`, and `babashka` coexist, so project layouts vary
**The class file carries a published promise**: Clojure reaches consumers as JVM bytecode [@javaJLS]

**Serialized objects cross on a published promise**: the stream carries the format version and a per-class serial version UID, and the specification states the current protocol is fully backward and forward compatible, read by JDK 1.1.7 and later [@javaSerSpec]

evolution.text: **The core language changes conservatively**: New capability usually arrives as a library, so `clojure.core` stays stable
**Old code keeps running**: Releases add functions and rarely remove or change existing behaviour
**Reader conditionals support one source for several hosts**: A `.cljc` file keeps shared code current across Clojure and ClojureScript
**A new JDK is a platform event**: Running on a newer Java release follows the JVM's schedule, not Clojure's
**Build variants multiply**: reader conditionals (#?(:clj ... :cljs ...)) select which forms read for each target

domain.text: **Excellent for web services**: Ring, Compojure, and Reitit express HTTP handling in plain functions and data
**Excellent for data processing**: Transducers and `core.async` pipelines process sequences and streams without intermediate collections
**The REPL suits exploratory and interactive work**: The running image allows a function to be redefined and retried immediately
**ClojureScript reaches the browser**: One language covers frontend and backend
**Less common for systems and numeric work**: No native memory control and no static numeric types make it unusual for kernels and HPC

learning.text: **The learning curve is steep**: It combines Lisp syntax, functional programming, and JVM integration in one language
**The core is small and consistent**: `clojure.core` fits in a reference page, and one data model applies everywhere
**The REPL gives immediate feedback**: A form is evaluated at once and its value is visible
**Macro writing is a second step**: Understanding expansion and hygiene takes practice beyond ordinary functions
**Stack traces cross into the JVM**: A failure reports Java frames and reader positions together

syntax.text: **Parenthesised forms are uniform**: Code and data share the S-expression representation, so there is no grammar beyond lists
**Prefix notation removes precedence rules**: `(+ 1 2)` puts the operator first everywhere
**Few special forms**: `let`, `fn`, `def`, `if`, `do`, and `quote` cover most of the core
**Delimiters are dense**: Deep nesting is hard to read without an editor that matches parentheses
**Threading and reader macros add notation**: `->`, `->>`, `#()`, and `@` are terse and must be learned

testing.text: **`clojure.test` is in the core library**: `deftest`, `is`, and `testing` need no external dependency
**A test runs against the live image**: Code can be redefined and a test re-run without a restart
**`clojure.spec` supports generative testing**: `clojure.spec.test.alpha/check` generates inputs from a spec and validates the results
**No compiler check finds a broken call site**: With dynamic typing the test suite, not the compiler, catches it

security.text: **Immutability limits accidental sharing**: A value cannot be mutated behind another holder's back
**No unsafe memory access in the language**: Clojure code cannot forge a pointer, and the JVM verifies bytecode
**The JVM's process and sandbox model applies**: A program runs under the host VM's isolation
**`eval` of constructed data is code execution**: `clojure.core/read-string` can run reader macros, so untrusted input must not reach `read` or `eval`
**A boundary check helps only where it is enabled**: A `spec` check runs when the program instruments or validates, not automatically

tradeoffs: **Dynamic typing is a deliberate trade**: No declarations speed construction and suit a REPL-first workflow, at the cost of run-time type checking
**Lisp syntax is the price of homoiconicity**: Parentheses and prefix notation buy code-as-data, which is what macros need
**Simple versus easy is a design value**: Hickey's distinction favours composable values over convenient wrappers, and that choice shapes the standard library rather than forcing a dependency
**A hosted language inherits its host's trade-offs**: JVM start-up and collection come from the platform choice, not from a mechanism of the language
**REPL-driven development assumes a running image**: The workflow favours exploration and interactive work, which is a team scope decision
**Clojure is not a systems language**: It assumes a host VM and a collector, which is a scope boundary rather than a defect
verdict: Clojure removes a large class of coupling in its own constructs: immutable values by default, protocols that add behaviour without a class hierarchy, atoms, refs, and agents for the three coordination styles, STM for coordinated change, and macros for extending syntax. Core coupling stays moderate because typing is dynamic, so a mismatch is caught at run time rather than at compile time, and because every value lives on a JVM heap with a collector. The platform and ecosystem dimension is the stronger half: full access to the JVM library base, a stable core, and ClojureScript for the browser, at the cost of JVM start-up, a library base smaller than Java's, and a steep combination of Lisp syntax, functional style, and JVM integration.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Moderate training data: models write it competently, with measurable language-specific weakness [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: The class-file format and the binary compatibility rules are published by the JVM specification

data_formats.note: Java's serialization specification publishes the stream protocol: the stream carries the magic number and version, every class descriptor carries a serial version UID, the writer can select a protocol version, the current protocol is stated fully backward and forward compatible, and JDK 1.1.7 and later read both protocol versions
